title: Monoidal resolution of characteristic monoids
statement: Let $(X,M)$ be a fine saturated log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] whose underlying scheme is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]; quasi-compact means every open cover has a finite subcover. Suppose every group $\overline M_{\bar x}^{\rm gp}$ is torsion free. Then there exist an integer $n\geq0$ and a finite tower $(X_n,M_n)\to\cdots\to(X_0,M_0)=(X,M)$ of saturated log blowups along nonempty coherent log ideals such that every characteristic monoid $\overline M_{n,\bar x}$ is isomorphic to $\mathbf N^{r(\bar x)}$ for some finite integer $r(\bar x)\geq0$. This assertion requires neither log regularity nor regularity of the strata.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.3.14--Theorem 3.3.15, printed p. 109 and proof pp. 109--110, with the saturated fan desingularization constructed in 3.1.27 and 3.2.19--3.2.21, printed pp. 102 and 105--106. The auxiliary toric resolution is taken over Q; the resulting monoidal construction has no characteristic restriction on X.

proof.text: Choose once and for all the smooth-functorial saturated fan desingularization $\mathcal R$ of [lem-trf-functorial-fan-desingularization]. For any of the log schemes under consideration, [lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup](i) supplies a finite strict etale chart cover by quasi-compact schemes with saturated torsion-free affine fans. Its hypotheses are exactly fs, quasi-compact, locally Noetherian and torsion-free characteristic groups, which are assumed in the item. The auxiliary characteristic-zero toric varieties used to construct $\mathcal R$ belong only to the proof of the fan theorem: we do not base change $X$ to $\mathbf Q$.

First work with a global fan chart $c:(V,\overline N)\to F$. Form the finite fan tower $\mathcal R(F)$ and pull it back using [lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup](ii). Explicitly, start at $(V_0,N_0)=(V,N)$ with chart $c_0=c$; if $F_{i+1}\to F_i$ has center $J_i$, blow up the log ideal which is the inverse image in $N_i$ of $c_i^{-1}J_i\,\overline N_i$. The cited construction gives the next fs log scheme and its chart to $F_{i+1}$, so induction runs through the finite index set of $\mathcal R(F)$. Each center is nonempty and coherent. Delete the stages with the whole log monoid as center. That ideal is generated by the unit, so its pullback is invertible under every fs log morphism. The identity therefore satisfies the universal property in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]; uniqueness over the base identifies its blowup with the identity. Denote the resulting contracted tower by $\mathcal T_c(V,N)$.

The local tower is independent of the chart. For two charts $c,d$ of the same $(V,N)$, apply [lem-trf-strict-fan-chart-local-comparison] to the identity strict morphism. Around every point they factor through isomorphic affine localizations of their target fans. The functoriality in [lem-trf-functorial-fan-desingularization] identifies the resolution on each localization with the contracted restriction of the resolution on the original fan and identifies the two localized resolutions through that isomorphism. Pulling their centers back by the equal chart maps gives the same ideals and, by [lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup](ii), the same log blowup towers on that neighborhood. These are canonical comparisons: the same ideal gives universal objects uniquely isomorphic as log schemes over the preceding stage, by [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Consequently comparisons agree on further restrictions and satisfy the cocycle identities; chart independence is an equality of locally specified ordered centers and towers, not just an isomorphism of final schemes.

source.place: VIII proof of Theorem 3.3.15, p.109, localization/comparison paragraph.

proof.text: For a strict etale map between globally charted log schemes, the same [lem-trf-strict-fan-chart-local-comparison] compares the source chart with the target chart pulled back along the map. Strict pullback compatibility in [lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup](ii) and smooth functoriality of [lem-trf-functorial-fan-desingularization] therefore identify the assigned source tower with the contracted pullback of the target tower. The identifications preserve the ideals at every stage, and their composition is the identification obtained by pulling back the same ideals along the composite. Apply this also to finite disjoint unions of charted log schemes, charted by the disjoint union of their fans. Functoriality for component inclusions gives the required compatibility for these unions. Thus the local assignment satisfies all the comparison and finite-union hypotheses of [lem-trf-functorial-log-blowup-etale-descent].

source.place: VIII proof of Theorem 3.3.15, pp.109--110, local comparison and finite disjoint unions.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-functorial-log-blowup-etale-descent] to this chart-independent rule and to $(X,M)$. It produces a finite tower $(X_n,M_n)\to\cdots\to(X,M)$ of saturated log blowups with nonempty coherent log ideal centers. The descent statement concerns the ordered towers and their centers, including deletion of whole-monoid centers; it supplies both the effectivity and finiteness needed here, rather than merely descent of the final log scheme.

source.place: VIII proof of Theorem 3.3.15, pp.109--110, descent reduction.

proof.text: Check the last characteristic monoids on the chart cover. On a chart $c$ the contracted pullback of the global tower is $c^*\mathcal R(F)$, by the descent conclusion. Contraction removes identity stages, so does not change the last log scheme. At a geometric point of its last stage, [lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup](ii) identifies its characteristic monoid with the stalk on the last fan of $\mathcal R(F)$; [lem-trf-functorial-fan-desingularization] says this stalk is $\mathbf N^r$ for finite $r\geq0$. Strict etale pullback identifies characteristic stalks, so the same holds at every geometric point of $X_n$. This argument uses only the characteristic monoids and charts, and invokes no log regularity or regularity of a stratum. The empty scheme and a zero-length tower cause no exception: the condition on points is vacuous in the former case, and the latter simply retains already free characteristic monoids.
